title: Uppsala UB C 513 (DECODE R4349): the ciphered colophon of the Strängnäs sequentiary, 1517, and the six-sign close of a Swedish note pasted on f. 1r

documents.shelfmark: Uppsala universitetsbibliotek, C 513, f. 19v (Alvin record 193385, attachment 42; DECODE R4349)
documents.route: Colophon of a Dominican scribe, Strängnäs convent, for the Västerås convent; not a letter

plaintext.source: Andersson-Schmitt, Hallberg & Hedlund, Mittelalterliche Handschriften der Universitätsbibliothek Uppsala, Bd. 5 (1992), pp. 275-276, entry C 513; the catalogue page is the PDF attached to DECODE R4349

transcription.source: Alvin full-resolution TIFF of f. 19v (attachment 42), four text lines under the chant notation
transcription.notes: Measured with --letters: the hyphens at two line ends are not counted. The minims of 'Annp' are ambiguous (m or nn); the catalogue's nn is kept. In both 'cpnxfntx' the n is partly a macron over cp.

documents.shelfmark: Uppsala universitetsbibliotek, C 513, slip pasted on f. 1r (Alvin record 193385, attachment 3; DECODE R4349)
documents.route: Unnamed writer to Anders Larsson (in the brewhouse), a short private note sent with medicines

transcription.source: Alvin full TIFF of f. 1r (attachment 3); clear text in slip.txt, signs in signs.txt
transcription.notes: The six signs look like cursive letters of the same hand: ÿ, ɑ, M, ÿ, u (or m), ꝺ (the hand's looped d).

system.summary: Vowel shift: each vowel is written as the next letter of the alphabet (a→b, e→f, i→k, o→p, u→x), consonants plain, word division kept.
system.notes: Plain consonants b and p also occur (liber, scriptus, presens, pro), so cipher b and p are each two-valued; context decides. The rubricated initial A of Anno is not enciphered. The words are set under chant notation as part of the book. The second piece, six signs closing the f. 1r slip, is of unknown system (probably a concealed signature).

prior_solution.where: Uppsala C-collection catalogue Bd. 5 (1992), entry C 513, gives the rule and the full reading; the catalogue page is attached to the DECODE record itself

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: n-gram language model (lang/ la) beam search for two-valued letters

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R4349 with the shared cookie: the only image is a placeholder icon; the attached PDF is two pages of the Uppsala C-collection catalogue describing C 513.
The catalogue entry states that the book is dated in secret script on f. 19v, each vowel replaced by the following consonant ('Annp dpmknk' = Anno domini), and prints the full reading.
Located f. 19v in the Alvin scans (attachment 42; attachment 40 is f. 18v) and downloaded the full TIFF.
Transcribed the four ciphered lines letter by letter (125 letters, 19 words with two line-end hyphens).
Applied the inverse shift, first word by word under the Latin model: k and x were misjudged because the model folds k into c, and prp came out as oro.
Fixed k=i and x=u (neither is a consonant in the text) and chose b/f/p by beam search over the whole colophon: the output matches the catalogue's reading word for word, prp = pro in context.

Prompted by the stop hook, checked all 175 Alvin images of C 513 for DECODE's 'six symbols in a note'. Back pastedown: clear pen trials only. Front: a pasted Old Swedish note to Anders Larsson ending in six signs.
Transcribed the slip's clear Old Swedish text (herbs and cinnamon bark sent for Anders Larsson's chest) and the six signs ÿ ɑ M ÿ u ꝺ.
Applied the colophon's vowel shift to the six signs: none of b f k p x occurs, so it does not fit.
Tried all 23 alphabet shifts on five readings of the signs (yamyud, yamymd, yanyud, yamynd, iamiud) and plain abbreviation (initials, closing formula): nothing.

outcome.method_basis: The Uppsala C-collection catalogue (1992), attached to DECODE R4349 itself, gives the vowel-to-next-letter rule and the full reading of the f. 19v colophon; the rule was applied to a new transcription and the output matched the printed reading word for word.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading.txt and signs.txt, cipher tokens: 125 colophon letters read, 6 slip signs unread
outcome.notes: Colophon read in the Uppsala catalogue (1992), checked on a new transcription. The six signs on the f. 1r slip, which DECODE's note means, are not read: too short. Added here: both transcriptions, the slip's text, the exact vowel-shift rule, and DECODE corrections.

gaps.item: the six signs closing the f. 1r slip (ÿ ɑ M ÿ u ꝺ)
gaps.detail: six signs, no key, no sibling in the same hand, no crib
